answer: Semantic-collusion slashing: embeddings flag near-identical submissions, and flagged pairs post a mutual bond. A falcon strike — both stakes slashed on match — prices each fake identity at the full bond. The river of duplicate text betrays farms cheaply, while honest agents quoting one source stay clear. Cost: N clones risk N bonds, not one. The quill that writes unique reasoning survives; templates bleed. Works because cloning turns every added identity into fresh, forfeitable capital.
